prose:knot-periodic-table:
Knot-periodic table of the elements.

Every neutral atom is a composite knot configuration built from protons, neutrons, and electrons via the three generation operations (knot-particle generation). The knot formula for an atom with Z protons and N neutrons is

  Z\mathfrak{p}  \oplus  N\mathfrak{n}
   \oplus  Z \cdot e^-

where \mathfrak{p} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H is the proton (color-linked quark triple), \mathfrak{n} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d}]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H is the neutron, e^- is the electron, the closure of the word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3 (the positive Hopf link T(2,2); the trefoil T_{2,3} is the single-component alternative model), and \oplus denotes Hopf linking. Here Z is the atomic number (proton count) and N is the neutron count, with A = Z + N the mass number. Throughout, fraktur letters name particles (\mathfrak{p} the proton, \mathfrak{n} the neutron, with \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d} their quark constituents).

Mass formula.

  \mathfrak{m}(Z, N) = 
  Z \cdot m_{\mathfrak{p}}
  +  N \cdot m_{\mathfrak{n}}
  -  (Z + N) \cdot (B/A)
  +  Z \cdot m_e

where m_{\mathfrak{p}} = \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}} + 2\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}} and m_{\mathfrak{n}} = 2\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}} + \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}} are the nucleon masses from the pair Skein formula (pair Skein mass formula), B/A is the binding energy per nucleon from the Skein polynomial of the multi-nucleon Hopf link (AME2020 values used here), and m_e \approx 0.511 MeV is the electron mass.

All individual knot types satisfy the embeddability closure (embeddability closure): every constituent has Seifert genus \leq 4 and descends to the base manifold. The generation completeness theorem (generation completeness) guarantees that every knot with genus \leq 4 is reachable from the seven torus generators via Skein crossing changes, so the particle spectrum tabulated below is complete over embeddable knots.

Transfer matrix computation.

The binding energy B/A and the nuclear Skein polynomial P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) are computed via transfer matrices (transfer matrix operator). Each nucleon pair (i, j) contributes a 2 \times 2 transfer matrix T_{ij}(q) with crossing coefficients determined by the pair type (\mathfrak{p}-\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n}-\mathfrak{n}, or mixed). The nuclear Skein polynomial in factored form (Skein polynomial) is:

  P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)
  = 
  \prod_{i=0}^{A-2} \hat{V}_i(q)

computed by exactly \binom{A}{2} transfer matrix multiplications (one per nucleon pair), with polynomial degree \leq A^2 - 1. The factored form is never expanded — each factor \hat{V}_i(q) is a rational function in q^{1/2} obtained from a chain of 2 \times 2 matrix products. The step count ranges from trivial ({}^{1}\mathrm{H}: 0 steps) to cheap at the heavy end: {}^{56}\mathrm{Fe} takes 1540 steps (degree \leq 3135) and {}^{238}\mathrm{U} takes 28203 steps (degree \leq 56643) — all evaluated in milliseconds.

Electron shell structure.

The orbital shells in the table arise from the eigenvalues of the photon-electron transfer matrix T_{\gamma e}(q) (shell structure eigenvalues). At the substrate parameter q, the dominant eigenvalue \lambda_+ = 1.1073 governs shell energy scaling via the Chebyshev recurrence \hat{V}(n+1, q) = (q - q^{-1}) \hat{V}(n, q) + \hat{V}(n-1, q), reproducing the Rydberg formula \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} \propto \lambda_+^{-n} \approx 1/n^2 for low shells. Sub-shell structure (s, p, d, f with capacities 2, 6, 10, 14) is formulated on the single-component T_{2,3} normal-bundle model (normal-bundle orbital space); on the primary two-component T(2,2) closure of the stabilised electron braids e_n \in B_{n+2} (shell--writhe correspondence), the corresponding two-component orbital multiplicity and 1/n^2 energy derivations remain open.

Beta decay universality.

Beta transitions between table entries are governed by a single universal matrix \Delta_\beta(q) (beta decay matrix): the same 2 \times 2 perturbation for every nucleus, regardless of partner nucleon type. The Q-value of any decay is the difference of parent and daughter Skein polynomials, concentrated at the converting nucleon's generators.

Neutron excess N > Z for heavy elements. In the QOU framework, proton--proton Hopf crossings carry a repulsive Skein phase (electromagnetic charge), while proton--neutron and neutron--neutron crossings are purely attractive (strong force only), so heavy nuclei must acquire extra neutrons to stay bound. The neutron count N therefore exceeds Z for all elements beyond calcium: the repulsive crossing penalty grows as \sim Z^2, requiring additional neutrons to stabilize the multi-nucleon link. Elements marked \diamond have a proton stability pair; those marked \star have a neutron stability pair. At these values the Skein polynomial has closed-shell structure with anomalously high B/A.

Stability pairs: 2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82 (protons); 2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126 (neutrons).

Knot-particle identification. The torus-family constituents are classified by the fermion--boson decomposition (fermions are knots, bosons are links). Proton and neutron quarks are Borromean-linked unknot strands (Borromean baryon), and nuclear binding comes from Hopf link crossings. The electron is the three-strand word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the positive Hopf link T(2,2); that decomposition covers the two-strand T(2,n) family only, so it does not decide the electron's statistics, which remain open. The trefoil T_{2,3} is the single-component alternative model of the electron. The full building-block catalogue with Jones polynomials and volumes is in (building-block knots).

Column key. N_{\mathrm{pred}} = predicted N from beta-stability formula (beta-stability), \Delta = |N - N_{\mathrm{pred}}|, k_\alpha = closed \alpha sub-links (= \min(\lfloor Z/2 \rfloor, \lfloor N/2 \rfloor)), M_q = QOU predicted mass, M_o = observed mass. \diamond = proton stability pair, \star = neutron stability pair. All masses in MeV/c^2. M_q computed at q = q_0; M_o from AME2020 nuclear masses plus Z \cdot m_e. B/A (MeV) from AME2020. The most stable (longest-lived) isotope is listed for each element.

Knot exhaustiveness. Detection is complete: every irreducible summand is labeled by a knot via Alexander surjectivity and Markov non-degeneracy (knot exhaustiveness). Generation is complete: every knot with genus \leq 4 is reachable (generation completeness). Faithfulness (whether distinct knots always give distinct Jones polynomials) remains an open question, but QOU uses Jones only for detection, not classification.

sec:knot-centric-table-intro:
The conventional periodic table indexes each element by its atomic number Z and electron configuration, an ordering imposed from outside the object it catalogues. In the present framework an element is a knot: a nuclear Borromean shell structure dressed by electrons, the level words e_n = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_n of its occupied shells. Its most natural label is therefore intrinsic — the braid whose closure realizes that knot — and organizing the table knot-centrically replaces the external atomic-number bookkeeping with the element's own topological data.

Reading the table from its simplest cell makes the scheme concrete. Hydrogen occupies the first cell of the first row (the N = 0 harmonic-oscillator shell), where the nuclear side carries a single Borromean unit; heavier elements are built by adding shells to this seed. Each element is then indexed by its braid representative together with its Hecke level, and the grid arranges these indices so that rows track the nuclear harmonic-oscillator level N and columns track the proton sub-shell filling order.
rem:knot-centric-table:
Remark Knot-centric periodic table: reorganization by nuclear and electronic knot structure. The standard periodic table organizes elements by electron configuration (rows = periods, columns = groups). A knot-centric periodic table reorganizes by the underlying knot topology: nuclear Borromean shell structure and the electron level words e_n = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_n. Under this reorganization shell structure and magic numbers become emergent: they follow from the Borromean crossing count rather than being read off an empirical table.

Organizing principles.

  1. Rows: nuclear HO level N with magic splits (shell-transition knot). Each row boundary is a magic number (stability pair).

  2. Columns: proton sub-shell filling order (Mayer--Jensen), left to right, with sub-shells separated by gaps and elements filling sequentially by Z within each sub-shell (the left-to-right magic-receptive-to-magic pattern is detailed under Column structure below).

    The sub-shell capacities follow the spin-orbit splitting of the harmonic oscillator levels (shell-transition knot): each sub-level nl_j accommodates 2j + 1 protons. The electron shell structure is determined by the eigenvalues of the photon-electron transfer matrix T_{\gamma e}(q) (shell structure eigenvalues): at the substrate parameter q, the larger eigenvalue \lambda_+ \approx 1.1073 governs shell energy scaling via a Chebyshev recurrence.

  3. Color coding: k_\alpha (number of \alpha sub-links in the nucleus), magic-receptive status (whether the element is in a spin-orbit magic shell).

Row structure (nuclear side).

See Table 1.

Rows 1--3 close at pure HO shell boundaries. Rows 4--7 are magic shells created by spin-orbit coupling (\mathcal{B}_3 crossing number = 3): the highest-j sub-level drops into the previous HO shell, creating a new stability pair. Elements in these rows are magic-receptive — they fill the spin-orbit-split sub-shell that leads to the next magic number.

Column structure (proton sub-shell filling).

Within each row, elements fill left to right through the Mayer--Jensen sub-shells. The sub-shell sequence for each row is:

See Table 2.

Each sub-shell group is separated by a gap in the grid. The first element in a row (far left) is the magic-receptive element — the first proton past the previous stability pair. The last element (far right) is the magic number that closes the shell.

Transfer matrix backbone.

The computational backbone of the table is the transfer matrix product (transfer matrix operator). Each nucleon pair contributes a 2 \times 2 matrix T_{ij}(q) with three crossing types:

See Table 3.

The nuclear Skein polynomial P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q) (Skein polynomial) is computed in factored form by \binom{A}{2} matrix multiplications. Beta decay shifts each crossing by the universal matrix \Delta_\beta(q) (beta decay matrix), independent of partner nucleon type.

Knot coverage.

The generation completeness theorem (generation completeness) guarantees that every knot with Seifert genus \leq 4 is reachable from the seven torus generators via Skein crossing changes. Detection is complete via Alexander surjectivity and Markov non-degeneracy (knot exhaustiveness).

Element card.

Each element displays:

  • Symbol and atomic number
  • Nuclear knot: Z\mathcal{B}_3 \oplus N\mathcal{B}_3 with k_\alpha sub-links highlighted
  • Electron knot: the level word e_n = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_n of the outermost occupied shell, whose writhe n + 2 gives the shell n
  • Transfer matrix data: \binom{A}{2} steps, \deg P_{\mathcal{N}} \leq A^2 - 1
  • Shell eigenvalues: dominant \lambda_+^n and Chebyshev index at the element's outermost shell
  • N_{\mathrm{pred}} vs N_{\mathrm{obs}}: predicted and observed neutron number
  • Magic-receptive indicator: a row labelled (magic-receptive) indicates the element is in a spin-orbit magic shell
rem:knot-centric-table-visualization-spe:
Remark Interactive visualization specification for the knot-centric periodic table. Where the static appendix table freezes the periodic structure at the observed substrate value, an interactive rendering lets a reader watch the row and shell structure deform continuously as q slides from 1 to q_0: the equal-width rows and absent magic shells at q = 1 reorganize into the observed table with its magic-receptive shells.

Visualization specification (for implementation).

The visualization should be an interactive HTML page (simulators/knot_periodic_table.html). Its feature groups fall into three physical layers the static table cannot expose side by side — the nuclear Borromean composition of each element, the shell structure of its electrons (the level words e_n), and the way both respond to the substrate parameter q — so the specification below unfolds from layout and tiles through the nuclear and electron panels to the q control that ties them together:

  1. Layout: 7 rows (one per stability-pair interval), vertically aligned on a shared grid. Columns follow Mayer--Jensen proton sub-shell filling order, with gaps between sub-shells.

  2. Element tiles: clickable tiles showing the element symbol, Z, N, k_\alpha, and a small SVG of the nuclear Borromean structure.

  3. Nuclear side panel: when an element is selected, show the full Borromean baryon composition:

    • Number of \alpha clusters (k_\alpha)
    • Which HO level the last nucleon occupies
    • Whether it's in a magic-receptive shell
    • Stability pair membership (\diamond, \star)

  4. Electron side panel: show the electron level word:

    • Current shell n and sub-shell \ell
    • The level word e_n = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_n and its writhe n + 2
    • Visual: the closure of e_n, starting from the Hopf link at n = 1, linked to a Borromean anchor

  5. Controls:

    • Toggle between standard and knot-centric layouts
    • Filter by stability pair, magic-receptive status, k_\alpha
    • q slider to show how the table changes with substrate parameter (at q = 1: all rows equal width, no magic shells; at q = q_0: observed table)

  6. Knot notation: use the visual conventions from knot atom diagrams:

    • Solid glyph = forward-time particle
    • Outlined glyph = backward-time (antiparticle)
    • Circle = unknot (neutrino)
    • Interlocked circles = Hopf link
    • Borromean symbol = 3 interlocked rings (quark composite)

  7. Data source: read from the knot-periodic table (knot-periodic table) for Z, N, N_{\mathrm{pred}}, \Delta N, k_\alpha, masses, and B/A.

  8. Transfer matrix overlay: optional display mode showing the number of transfer matrix steps \binom{A}{2} and Skein polynomial degree bound A^2 - 1 for each element, color-coded by computational complexity.

  9. Shell eigenvalue display: optional overlay showing \lambda_+^n at the element's outermost electron shell, with the Chebyshev recurrence index and binding energy \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} \propto \lambda_+^{-n}.

Scope, Confinement-Layer Architecture, and Certification Contract.

The pre-Archimedean derivation chain (Pre-Archimedean derivation chain) reduces physical observables to algebraic invariants of braid closures, Temperley--Lieb trace quotients, and hyperbolic periods on the genus-four Bring surface \Sigma_4 (\chi(\Sigma_4) = -6). This annex specifies the non-standard computational and machine-certification procedures that evaluate those invariants across the five discrete confinement layers \mathcal{L}_0 \to \mathcal{L}_4: three-strand quark--gluon normal forms in H_3(q) (\mathcal{L}_0), nucleon braids, radical shadow prices, and Archimedean lepton/baryon resolvents (\mathcal{L}_1), multi-nucleon monotone Bratteli transfer sweeps and physical cluster-chamber reductions in H_{3A}(q) (\mathcal{L}_2), capacitated atomic shell promotions (\mathcal{L}_3), and molecular toric stoichiometry (\mathcal{L}_4).

Throughout this annex, standard external algorithms—completed Coxeter/Hecke Gröbner--Shirshov reduction, Young--Hoefsmit seminormal matrix representations, toric binomial Gröbner/Graver bases, and primal--dual interior-point conic solvers—are cited directly from the literature together with their exact parameter pins in this model: unimodular skein parameter h = q - q^{-1} (\sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1) and Markov trace weight z = q^3/(q^2+1) on the faithful Temperley--Lieb quotient TL_n(q) = H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad}\,\tau_q. Symbolic stages operate exactly over \mathbb{Q}(q) or linearly ordered commutative rings, while every Archimedean evaluation past the comparison boundary is executed in 80-decimal-place arbitrary-precision arithmetic (truncation bound \le 10^{-60}, with zero IEEE-754 binary64 intermediates) from the three physical calibration observables (m_e, \mathfrak{D}_\beta, m_\pi) (Three-calibration discipline).

sec:tm-notation-intro:
Transfer matrices carrying the paper's nuclear computations are scattered across chapters. This appendix gathers them so any transfer matrix can be looked up in explicit closed form. Recurring symbols include the substrate parameter q, the braid/Hecke generators \sigma_i, the transfer matrices T_{K_1,K_2}, and the Markov parameter z(q).

Every transfer matrix is indexed by the pair of knots (K_1, K_2) meeting at a crossing. The symbol T_{K_1,K_2}(q) names the matrix before any general scheme is stated.

The tables below set out the symbol glossary, the knot dictionary, particle assignments, and nucleon labels, followed by the mechanism relating them.
tm-notation:
Notation and conventions.

This appendix is self-contained: every transfer matrix appears in explicit closed form, with notation defined locally.

Symbols are collected in Table 1. Every transfer matrix is labelled by a pair of knots (K_1, K_2) meeting at a crossing. The relevant knots and their labels are listed in Table 2. Particle assignments for each knot type are in Table 3. Knot assignments for the proton and neutron are given in Table 4.

The per-crossing transfer matrices are composed across a nucleus to produce a single scalar, its nuclear Skein polynomial P_{\mathcal{N}}(q).

Given a nucleus with A = Z + N nucleons, the braid word has A - 1 generators \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{A-2}. At each generator \sigma_i, the transfer matrices of all crossings are composed as operators acting by left-multiplication, applied from right to left in the braid word:

  M_i(q) = \prod_{j=A-1}^{i+1} T_{K_j, K_i}(q)

The product is taken in decreasing order of j. The Markov-traced volume at generator \sigma_i is

  \hat{V}_i(q) = z(q) \cdot (M_i)_{11} + (M_i)_{21}

where z(q) = q^3/(q^2+1) = q^2/[2]_q is the Markov-trace loop weight (\mathrm{tr}_M(e_i) = q - z(q) = 1/[2]_q for e_i = q - \sigma_i). Every symbolic factor \hat{V}_i(q) and nuclear Skein polynomial P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) below uses this rational weight; exact 80-digit numerical evaluations at q_0^{(p)} appear in Table A.3. The nuclear Skein polynomial is:

  P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) = \prod_{i=0}^{A-2} \hat{V}_i(q)

This requires exactly \binom{A}{2} transfer matrix multiplications.

tm-general-form:
The general transfer matrix.

A general form collapses every crossing type into a single two-parameter family. The three nuclear crossings and the connected-sum case become special points of one matrix. Every transfer matrix has the same 2 \times 2 structure, parameterized by two crossing coefficients (c, d):

  T(c, d) = \begin{pmatrix} c(q - q^{-1}) + d & c \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}

The coefficients (c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] depend on how the two knots interact. For knots meeting via connected sum, the Jones polynomial satisfies J_{K_1 \# K_2} = J_{K_1} \cdot J_{K_2}, giving c = 1 and d = 0. For knots meeting via the Hecke product (the physically relevant case for nucleon crossings), the coefficients are determined by the representation-theoretic structure of the crossing. They do not reduce to connected-sum formulas. The three nuclear crossing types have specific (c, d) values listed in Section 3.2.

The transfer matrix acts on a Iwahori--Hecke algebra element a\sigma_i + b by left multiplication and Hecke reduction (T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1):

  \begin{pmatrix} a' \\ b' \end{pmatrix} = T(c, d) \cdot \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix}

Explicitly:

  a' = ac(q - q^{-1}) + ad + bc, \qquad b' = ac + bd

Three properties fix how the crossing acts: its determinant controls invertibility, its eigenvalues control spectral behavior under iteration, and its degenerate limits recover the connected-sum and scalar matrices.

Determinant. The determinant governs whether the crossing action is invertible:

  \det T(c, d) = cd(q - q^{-1}) + d^2 - c^2

Eigenvalues (when c \neq 0). The eigenvalues give the spectral behavior of the crossing under repeated application:

  \lambda_{\pm} = \frac{1}{2}\Bigl[c(q - q^{-1}) + 2d \pm \sqrt{\bigl[c(q - q^{-1})\bigr]^2 + 4c^2}\Bigr]

Special cases. The two degenerations of interest recover matrices met earlier: c = 0 collapses T to the scalar matrix, while c = 1, d = 0 gives the connected-sum (fundamental) matrix.

  • c = 0: T(0, d) = d \cdot \mathbb{I} (scalar matrix)
  • d = 0: T(c, 0) = c \cdot \begin{pmatrix} q - q^{-1} & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}
  • c = 1, d = 0: The fundamental matrix T_{pp}
sec:tm-knot-pairs-intro:
Every interaction in this framework is a crossing between two knotted strands. The knot polynomial that records such a crossing is an unbounded object whose degree grows with knot complexity. A transfer matrix trades this unbounded data for a fixed-size operator: to each pair of knots one assigns a 2 \times 2 matrix over \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]. This compresses the polynomial content into four Laurent-polynomial entries obtained from the Hecke reduction. The payoff is composition: because every crossing carries a matrix of the same shape, a chain of crossings becomes a matrix product, and interactions of very different physical character can be iterated on equal footing.

The smallest case makes the compression visible. Two unknotted strands (the vacuum--vacuum pair) carry no knotting at all, yet their crossing does not reduce to the identity. The Hecke relation still fires, producing the simplest non-identity transfer matrix. That a genuinely empty configuration produces a non-trivial matrix indicates the transfer matrix records the crossing itself, not merely the knots.

This section builds the catalogue crossing type by crossing type. It begins with the trivial matrices, passes to the nuclear matrices, then to the electromagnetic matrices, and closes by sorting the entire list into a short classification.
tm-knot-pairs:
Transfer matrices of knot pairs.

A transfer matrix records how a single crossing between two knotted strands acts on the Hecke chain. Each knot pair contributes a 2 \times 2 block determined by its crossing coefficients c and d. Every nuclear and electromagnetic crossing reduces to one of just three classes (Section 5). This section lists every transfer matrix for each knot pair over \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}].

sec:tm-interactions-intro:
A transfer matrix records a single configuration of interacting braid strands; an interaction is a change from one such configuration to another. Since every crossing type carries a transfer matrix, the change an interaction induces is simply the difference between the matrix after the interaction and the matrix before it. This encodes disparate processes—beta decay, photon absorption, pair creation—as a single operator on a 2 \times 2 matrix, so they can be compared and iterated.

Converting one neutron into a proton advances a nuclear crossing type by one step—from T_{nn} to T_{\mathrm{mix}}—and the change is the difference \Delta = T_{\mathrm{after}} - T_{\mathrm{before}}. Writing this difference as an operator makes the interaction itself the object of study. This section builds the catalogue of such operators.
tm-interactions:
Interaction and decay matrices.

This appendix collects the transfer-matrix changes induced by elementary processes. An interaction changing the crossing type from (K_1, K_2) to (K_1', K_2') is encoded by the \Delta operator:

  \Delta_{K_1 K_2 \to K_1' K_2'}(q) = T_{K_1', K_2'}(q) - T_{K_1, K_2}(q)

These entries are the amplitudes of the 2\times 2 Toffoli transfer matrix \mathbf{M}(q), resolved by parity channel: index 6 labels the even sector and index 7 the odd sector. The diagonal amplitudes P_{6,6} and P_{7,7} are the no-flip (parity-preserving) amplitudes in the even and odd channels; the off-diagonal P_{7,6} is the target-flip amplitude and P_{6,7} its reverse, evaluated at the Markov trace weight z = q^3/(q^2+1) throughout.

Entry Formula
P_{6,6} (no flip, even) \dfrac{(q^4+1)(q^4+q^2+2)}{4q(q^2+1)^2}
P_{7,7} (no flip, odd) \dfrac{q^3(q^4+1)}{(q^2+1)^2}
P_{7,6} (flip) -\dfrac{(q-1)(q+1)(q^6+q^4+2q^2+1)}{2q(q^2+1)^2}
P_{6,7} (reverse flip) \dfrac{(q-1)(q+1)(2q^6+q^4+q^2+1)}{2q(q^2+1)^2}

The flip channel is not antisymmetric. One might expect P_{6,7} = -P_{7,6}, on the grounds that reversing the crossing negates it. The two derived amplitudes differ by more than a sign — their sextic factors are q^6+q^4+2q^2+1 and 2q^6+q^4+q^2+1 — so P_{6,7} \neq -P_{7,6}. This structural asymmetry persists across every admissible choice of Markov trace weight. \Phi itself is withdrawn; it is not in the image of the Toffoli construction (Toffoli transfer matrix).
